transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mr. Park. Thank you for coming in. I need to tell you something about your medicine.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Hello doctor. Is something wrong?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. We made a mistake with your immunotherapy. This is the medicine that helps your body fight the cancer. We gave it to you on the wrong day.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wrong day? But I came when you told me to come.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. I put the date wrong on my calendar. Because of that, you got the dose too early in your cycle. This means the medicine might not work as well as it should.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. I do not... does that mean the cancer comes back? I am very scared.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Look, we need to focus on the facts. The error is that the timing was off. It is a calendar mistake. Do you understand what I mean by "wrong day"?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, I think so. But I am just... I am alone here, and I don't know if this is okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for any confusion this caused, but we were really busy last week with many patients.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to be healthy. I cannot tell my parents yet, they are in Korea and I don't want them to—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Sorry to jump in, but we have to move through this because I have to go to another appointment in a few minutes. We need to figure out the next step.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am sorry. I just... I feel very nervous.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But as I said, the problem was the date on the calendar. Your medicine was given on Tuesday instead of Friday. Does that part make sense to you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. It makes sense. But why did it happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, the calendar entry was wrong. It is a human error. Do you follow me so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I follow. Will the medicine still work?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It might be less effective. It is not guaranteed to fail, but the timing is important for the medicine to hit the cancer cells correctly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know what to do. I don't know if I should talk to a lawyer or... I don't know my rights here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let's not wrap up by talking about lawyers. Let's just look at the schedule.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel very small here. Everything is so fast.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But we have to keep moving.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Are you angry at me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, I am not angry. But we need to fix the plan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What is the plan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will probably change the date of your next dose.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will that be?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know the exact date yet. I will check the computer and we will see.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will you tell me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, just stay tuned for an email from the clinic. We will send you a message when we decide the new date.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An email? What if I don't see it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You have a phone, right? You will see it there.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I am very worried about my treatment.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Again, I understand. But we are moving forward now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is there anything I should do?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Not really. Just wait for that email.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will the doctor who is the head of the department know?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: They will be informed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I should have asked more questions when I was here last week.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Actually, let me stop you there. It wasn't your fault, it was the calendar. But like I said, I really have to go now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will email you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you, doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Goodbye.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('move through this', 'have to go', 'keep moving') and interrupts the patient during emotional disclosures.

E.justification: Error named in the second turn, lay language used throughout, and comprehension checked multiple times ('Do you understand...', 'Does that part make sense...').

A.justification: The apology is diluted by an immediate excuse regarding being 'really busy last week with many patients'.

R.justification: Resident uses generic validation ('I understand') but consistently redirects emotional bids back to factual calendar details.

T.justification: The plan consists of placeholders ('probably change the date', 'I don't know the exact date yet', 'stay tuned for an email').
